entry.title: Common Git Mistakes (And How to Fix Them)
entry.summary:
Even experienced developers make mistakes with Git. The good news is that most Git mistakes are recoverable if you know what to do. This post covers some of the most common Git problems and how to fix them safely. The mistake: main instead of a feature branch. The fix: git checkout -b feature-branch git reset --soft HEAD~1 git commit
This moves your commit onto a new branch without losing changes. The mistake: The fix: git checkout -b new-branch
Your work stays intact. The mistake: fix, update, or changes. The fix: git commit -m "Fix null pointer error in user login"
Good commit messages save time during reviews and debugging. The mistake: The fix: git rm --cached .env echo ".env" >> .gitignore git commit -m "Remove env file from repo"
If secrets were pushed, rotate them immediately. The mistake: The fix: <<<<<<< HEAD your code ======= their code >>>>>>> branch-name
Choose the correct logic, remove the markers, then: git add . git commit
The mistake: The fix: git revert <commit-hash>
Never rewrite shared history unless absolutely necessary. The mistake: The fix: git reflog
Find the commit and recover it: git checkout <commit-hash>
Git almost never truly deletes your work. The mistake: git push --force on a shared branch. The fix: git push --force-with-lease
This is safer and prevents overwriting others’ work. The mistake: The fix: git pull --rebase
This keeps history clean and avoids unnecessary merge commits. The mistake: The fix: One feature One fix One idea per commit Git mistakes happen to everyone, what matters is knowing how to recover. Once you understand how Git tracks history, it becomes a powerful safety net rather than a source of stress. Learn the tools, respect shared branches, and don’t panic, Git is usually on your side.

entry.title: How to Use UFW (Uncomplicated Firewall)
entry.summary:
Basic Penggunaan UFW di Ubuntu Server 24.04 Pada postingan ini saya akan membahas basic penggunaan UFW (Uncomplicated Firewall) pada Ubuntu Server 24.04. UFW adalah firewall bawaan Ubuntu/Debian yang berfungsi untuk mengatur lalu lintas jaringan (port dan IP) agar server menjadi lebih aman. ufw status
Secara default, pada instalasi baru Ubuntu Server, UFW belum aktif. ufw enable
Disable UFW ufw disable
Untuk membuka port tertentu, misalnya SSH (port 22): ufw allow 22/tcp
Allow Port dari IP Tertentu, jika ingin membatasi akses hanya dari satu IP tertentu, misalnya port 22 hanya boleh diakses dari IP 10.10.10.5: ufw allow from 10.10.10.5 to any port 22 proto tcp
Allow Port dari Satu Subnet, jika ingin mengizinkan satu subnet (misalnya prefix /24): ufw allow from 10.10.10.0/24 to any port 22 proto tcp
Untuk melihat semua rule yang sudah dibuat ufw status
Jika ingin melihat urutan rule, gunakan: ufw status numbered
Penghapusan rule menggunakan nomor urutan. 22 berada di urutan ke-2, maka perintahnya: ufw delete 2
Kurang lebih seperti itulah basic penggunaan UFW di Ubuntu Server. Postingan ini akan saya update seiring bertambahnya pengalaman dalam menggunakan UFW, sekaligus sebagai catatan dan dokumentasi pribadi. Selamat mencoba dan semoga bermanfaat

entry.summary: I make music mostly for content. Short videos, background tracks, loops for social posts. Speed matters more than perfection. Remove vocals for an instrumental cut Reuse drums in a different tempo Fix a bass line that felt too loud on mobile Re-recording was not realistic. I needed another option. Before touching any tool, I spent time understanding the basics. I tested stem splitting on three real tracks: A clean pop track with clear vocals A lo-fi beat with vinyl noise A dense EDM drop with heavy sidechain Results were mixed. That matched my experience almost perfectly. The real value wasn’t perfection. It was speed. AI Stem Splitter After some trial and error, I changed how I work: During this phase, I tried a few web-based tools. One of them was MusicArt. If you’re expecting studio-perfect stems, you’ll be disappointed. The mix is clean The goal is reuse, not perfection Time matters more than purity Used that way, it becomes less of a gimmick and more of a creative safety net. I used to think finishing a track meant closing the door on it. Now I treat exports as something I can reopen in different ways. Not perfectly. Not endlessly. But enough to keep ideas moving.
